title: Board search, screenshots and recording
changes: Pick up where you left off with previews of your three most recent boards, including boards shared with you.
Press Cmd+K on Mac or Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux to find tools, menu actions, board titles, or a phrase you remember writing.
Take a screenshot or record the board with tab audio, your microphone, both, or neither. Stop recording stays within reach.
Captures save to Media by default. Choose Don’t save in the preview to skip the upload, or Save locally to download a copy.
Accept word suggestions as you write, browse a site with collaborators, and press H for the Hand tool in either keyboard mode.

tour.title: Recognize your board
tour.body: On a blank board, look below the illustration for up to three previews. Names and initials identify shared boards. Open a card to return to it, or choose All boards for the full list.

tour.title: Find a board by what you wrote
tour.body: Open Search in the board menu or press <kbd>⌘K</kbd>. Try a word from a sticky note. Matching boards show an excerpt. You can also search for a tool or menu action.

tour.title: Finish a word as you type
tour.body: When a gray word ending appears, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>→</kbd> to accept it. Keep typing to use your own ending. You can turn writing help off in the menu.

tour.title: Read a page together
tour.body: On boards with shared browsing enabled, an editor can open the globe and enter a web address. Everyone can follow the page as it scrolls. Another editor can choose Take control.

tour.title: Keep a screenshot where you want it
tour.body: Open the camera on a saved board, frame your shot and choose Take screenshot. The preview saves to Media by default. Choose Don’t save to skip the upload, Save locally to download, or Copy for the clipboard.

tour.title: Choose what your recording hears
tour.body: In Chrome or Edge on a computer, open the camera and choose Video. Choose Tab audio, Microphone, or both. Press <kbd>⇧⌘S</kbd> to start or stop recording, or use the on-screen buttons.

tour.title: Pan with the Hand tool
tour.body: Press <kbd>H</kbd> and drag to move across the canvas. In Vim mode, <kbd>gh</kbd> now jumps to the item on the left and <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>H</kbd> still pans left.

title: Drawing, layout and touch
changes: Hold the pen still in Beautify mode to snap a sketch into a clean shape. Select several items to align them, space them evenly or tidy up their layout.
Pasted images appear while they upload. Select an image to change its corners from square to fully rounded.
On a phone, use one finger to draw and two to pan or zoom. The compact toolbar keeps all drawing tools within reach.
Invite previews show the board name. Voice chat shows how many people are in a call before you join.

tour.title: Draw a cleaner shape
tour.body: Turn on Beautify in the pen toolbar. Draw a rough circle and hold still before lifting the pen to snap it into shape.

tour.title: Line things up
tour.body: Select several items, open Align and space, then choose Tidy up to arrange them in rows with even gaps.

tour.title: Paste and round an image
tour.body: A pasted picture appears as it uploads. Select it and choose Rounded corners in its toolbar.

tour.title: Move with two fingers
tour.body: Spread two fingers to zoom. Move both fingers in the same direction to pan, then lift them and draw again with one finger.

tour.title: Recognize an invite
tour.body: Name the board before sharing it. Its title appears in the link preview when you paste an invite into a chat.

tour.title: See who is in voice
tour.body: The call count tells you how many people are already talking. You can also see active calls in All boards.

title: Text, saved views and collaboration
changes: Apply bold or underline to individual words, preview fonts by hovering, and resize selected text with + and −.
Save a board area as a named view. Open Views with gv, or choose Follow to see where a collaborator is working.
Adjust the pen and eraser in one-pixel steps. Erase just the ink under the brush or switch to whole strokes.
